name: workshop
words: how to author a craft in the Workshop — a draft under your seat, a graph that branches, the node inspector, the agent on your words, the cut as the gate
text: THE WORKSHOP (Phase 8 sp3, canon 0010) is the one place where all mutability occurs. Open it with “open the workshop” or load a craft straight into it: “load the librarian template in the workshop”, “load mind.v0 in the workshop”, “load my bob draft in the workshop”. The left rail finds earlier work: YOUR DRAFTS (under your seat alone — never on the shelf, never in any recall) and THE SHELF's crafts by kind, with a filter box. The canvas DRAWS THE DECLARATION: a graph's nodes as blocks (the entry ringed; think = the metered mind, echo = the words back; each node's prompt · skill · tools · mind refs as chips) and its ways out as arrows — an arrow with no `when` is the default (“otherwise”); a `when` is one of: the hull's edge the ask took (chat · work · event), a pattern in the ask's words, a pattern in the last reply. A node may have several ways out when at most one wears no `when`; the graph runs forward only (a loop refuses). Click a node for the NODE INSPECTOR: its id, kind, prompt (a prompt on the shelf), skill (a skill on the shelf), tools (narrowed from what the template declares — never widened), mind (a stall in the Stable); add a node after it, add a way out, remove it. Click an arrow to set or clear its `when`. The DECLARATION box below the canvas is the same truth as JSON — edit either, the other follows; SAVE writes the draft under your seat (routine, L1). A craft from the shelf opens read-only with its address, pin, version and WHERE IT STANDS (the bodies wearing it and the floor or room each stands on); “draft from this” copies it into a new draft of yours. THE AGENT: with the Workshop open the chat speaks to its agent, `workshop`; say “add an echo node after think” or “wire a way out of route to greet when the ask says hello” and it calls the draft tool with the whole declaration — the canvas redraws. THE MIND CHIP in the header assigns the Workshop agent's mind from the Stable's standing stalls (held at the interlock, L2); an Anthropic stall is Claude the model, metered like every mind — Claude the developer (repo access, the factories' hands) is Phase 9, not this chip. THE CUT IS YOURS: “cut the <name> draft” holds at the interlock; on your yes the draft lands on the shelf as version 1 or the next version (a sibling), probed at once, the draft spent. A resident's template asks your code (L3); firmware cuts only in a dev universe; an agent's template waits for the Experiment (spoonful 4). Floor and room are not chosen here: where a body's next life stands is a field on the promotion (spoonful 4); the Workshop shows where a craft's wearers stand today.
